subject.title: fix(chat): preserve PNG attachments in native clients

question: Should Android and Apple native chat surfaces preserve every PNG as a bounded PNG, or retain the shipped canonical-JPEG normalization policy?
rationale: Both policies are technically plausible: PNG preserves transparency and source fidelity, while canonical JPEG provides consistent transport behavior and generally better photo compression; current tests and merged history intentionally encode the JPEG policy, so automation cannot choose the replacement contract.

options.title: Preserve bounded PNGs
options.body: Approve source-format preservation for PNG across all three native send surfaces, contingent on real-device gateway proof for fidelity, metadata removal, and size bounds.

options.title: Preserve only alpha PNGs
options.body: Keep opaque images on the efficient JPEG path while retaining PNG only when conversion would destroy transparency.

options.title: Retain canonical JPEG
options.body: Keep the shipped normalization contract and close or narrow this PR rather than adding a second native output policy.

recommendation.title: Preserve bounded PNGs
recommendation.body: Approve source-format preservation for PNG across all three native send surfaces, contingent on real-device gateway proof for fidelity, metadata removal, and size bounds.

likelyOwner.reason: The current PR timeline provides the clearest direct routing signal for resolving the cross-platform product-policy choice.
